Docs changes (Material theme only, no custom theme):

  • Look: dark ink header and footer, cerulean links, and a navy dark mode that follows the system setting (with a toggle). Fonts are Inter and JetBrains Mono, with stronger headings, rounded code blocks and tables, breadcrumbs, and prev/next links at the bottom of each page.
  • Logo: a new mark, a sphere with open scattered wavefronts, used in the header and as the favicon.
  • Home page: lead line, two buttons, the treams credit as a callout, and cards for "What treams-rs adds" and "Where to go next". The gradients card was outdated (it only named the explicit adapter modules); it now says all four frameworks work through the ordinary API.
  • Bug fix: generated reference pages showed up as "Sw", "Treams rs", etc. in the nav and browser tab. They now read treams_rs.sw, treams_rs.special, and so on.
  • Removed: MathJax. It loaded from a CDN on every page, but no page uses math. Pages are otherwise unchanged.
  • Tables: I tried keeping identifiers in table cells from breaking mid-word, but that made 9 more tables overflow, so I left Material's default wrapping.

README:

  • Wordmark: built like Advect's, the mark plus "treams-rs" in Source Code Pro Bold, loaded from an absolute raw.githubusercontent.com URL so PyPI shows it. The URL points at main, so the image appears once the PR merges.
  • Install section: now gives the extras as commands (pip install "treams-rs[advect]", [io], …). pip install treams-rs was already there.

Advect has a PyPI bug you'll want to know about. Its wordmark switches colour using prefers-color-scheme inside the SVG. In an <img>, Chromium checks the OS setting, not the page. So anyone with a dark-mode OS sees near-white text on PyPI's white page; I reproduced this. For treams-rs I used two fixed-colour files in a <picture>. PyPI strips the <source> element, so it always shows the navy version. I haven't touched Advect.

On whether they're worth fixing: probably yes, but I'm basing that on the verifiers' reports, not on sizing the fixes myself.

  • 1-D chain is the stronger case: a plain crash under three frameworks on a valid, NumPy-accepted input.
  • lpmv mixed lists is a silent precision loss. In a float64 science library that's worse than it sounds, especially if the cause is shared PyTorch input conversion that other functions also use.

Both look small. I'll have each fixed and verified independently, and land them as one extra commit only if the fix turns out small and safe. In parallel I'll prepare the Advect README fix and PR.
